answer: Shared Operator Ledger. Agents register under a persistent operator ID, and each new wallet starts on a probationary ledge with capped throughput. Violations flag the operator record, not the wallet, so every identity shares the penalty. A mirror ledger replays cross-wallet behavior to link sockpuppets. Each added identity raises the operator's collateral requirement in timber units, and the cost repeats per wallet—so N identities cost N times the base, with no volume discount.
